newsitem.title: CANADA: Paddington Bear to make journey to Canada. [CORRECTED 20:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Paddington Bear to make journey to Canada. [CORRECTED 20:55 GMT]

text.p: Paddington Bear, the British childhood symbol that made a famous fictional journey to London's Paddington Station from deepest, darkest Peru (corrects from Africa), is moving to snowy Canada.

Montreal-based CINAR Films Inc. said on Thursday it plans to buy the FilmFair animation library and production facilities and animated series from Britain's Caspian Group Plc for 10.5 million British pounds ($17.1 million) in cash and stock.
Series in the library include such famous British cartoons as "Paddington Bear", "The Herbs" and "Simon in the Land of Chalk Drawings."
According to British media reports, Caspian is dumping the characters to focus on its sports franchises, including the Leeds United Football (soccer) Club, which it bought in July.
The shows, many of which stopped production in the late 1980s and early 1990s, are aired in up to 30 countries.
CINAR Chief Financial Officer Hasanain Panju said in a telephone interview that CINAR's 100-country distribution network can help bolster the revenue stream to the library.
"We intend to restore the prominence and reputation of the FilmFair Library to that enjoyed in the past," said CINAR President Ronald Weinberg.
CINAR will produce new episodes of some of the series in the library, but Panju declined to specify which ones.
The deal also gives CINAR the video, music publishing, licensing and merchandising rights to the series.
But Paddington Bear creator Michael Bond will retain part of the Paddington rights, Panju said.
